source.title: Common English words chosen for each age group (starter list). Meanings and sentences are original to this project.
source.license: Reference only (the page describes the kind of list this was modelled on). No list was copied: words, meanings and sentences were written for this project and are released with it.

words.meaning: needed, something you must have
words.sentence: It is necessary to wear a seatbelt.
words.tip: One collar and two sleeves: one c and two s.

words.meaning: kept apart, not joined together
words.sentence: Sort the recycling into separate bins.

words.meaning: without any doubt
words.sentence: It will definitely rain tomorrow.

words.meaning: the natural world and surroundings
words.sentence: Plastic waste harms the environment.

words.meaning: the people who run a country
words.sentence: The government announced a new law.

words.meaning: what you know through learning
words.sentence: Knowledge grows when you ask questions.

words.meaning: a chart of the days and months of a year
words.sentence: The exam is marked on the calendar.

words.meaning: to make someone feel awkward or ashamed
words.sentence: Please do not embarrass your brother.

words.meaning: a special event or time
words.sentence: Her birthday is a special occasion.

words.meaning: a place where you pay for a meal
words.sentence: The restaurant is busy on Fridays.

words.meaning: being away from a place
words.sentence: Her absence was noticed.

words.meaning: to succeed in doing something
words.sentence: Hard work helps you achieve your goals.
words.tip: I before e, except after c.

words.meaning: ready to attack or fight
words.sentence: The dog became aggressive when it was scared.

words.meaning: a strong wish to do or be something
words.sentence: Her ambition is to be a doctor.

words.meaning: easy to see or understand
words.sentence: It was apparent that he was tired.

words.meaning: the way a person or thing looks
words.sentence: His appearance changed after the haircut.

words.meaning: a disagreement, or a reason given for an idea
words.sentence: They had an argument about the rules.

words.meaning: a person who is good at sport
words.sentence: The athlete trained every day.

words.meaning: the people who watch or listen to a show
words.sentence: The audience clapped loudly.

words.meaning: the start of something
words.sentence: The beginning of the film was slow.

words.meaning: a line that marks the edge of something
words.sentence: The fence marks the boundary of the field.

words.meaning: a group of things of the same kind
words.sentence: Fruit is one category of food.

words.meaning: the top inside surface of a room
words.sentence: A spider crawled across the ceiling.

words.meaning: something difficult that tests your ability
words.sentence: The puzzle was a real challenge.

words.meaning: a person in a story, or the qualities that make a person who they are
words.sentence: My top character is the brave knight.

words.meaning: a person you work with
words.sentence: She asked a colleague for help.

words.meaning: a contest to see who is best
words.sentence: She won the swimming competition.

words.meaning: easy to use or reach
words.sentence: The shop is convenient because it is close.

words.meaning: saying what is wrong with something
words.sentence: He accepted the criticism calmly.

words.meaning: a strong wish to learn or know
words.sentence: Her curiosity made her read more.

words.meaning: a choice that you make
words.sentence: It was a hard decision.

words.meaning: a hard choice between two things
words.sentence: She faced a dilemma about which team to join.

words.meaning: to let someone down by not being as good as they hoped
words.sentence: I did not want to disappoint my coach.

words.meaning: training yourself to follow rules and keep trying
words.sentence: It takes discipline to train every day.

words.meaning: to mix into a liquid so that it cannot be seen
words.sentence: Sugar will dissolve in hot water.

words.meaning: great interest and excitement
words.sentence: She spoke with enthusiasm.

words.meaning: the tools and things needed for a job or sport
words.sentence: The team packed the equipment.

words.meaning: to make something sound bigger or better than it is
words.sentence: Do not exaggerate the story.

words.meaning: extremely good
words.sentence: Her work is excellent.

words.meaning: being real or alive
words.sentence: Scientists study the existence of life on other planets.

words.meaning: to provide room or space for
words.sentence: The hall can accommodate two hundred people.

words.meaning: a person who handles letters, calls and meetings for an office
words.sentence: The secretary booked the meeting.

words.meaning: a line of people waiting
words.sentence: A long queue formed at the door.

words.meaning: a repeating pattern of beats in music
words.sentence: The drummer kept a steady rhythm.
words.tip: Rhythm Helps Your Two Hips Move.

words.meaning: well known to you
words.sentence: That tune sounds familiar.

words.meaning: a special right or advantage
words.sentence: Voting is a privilege and a responsibility.

words.meaning: a space with no air in it
words.sentence: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

words.meaning: playfully naughty
words.sentence: The mischievous puppy hid my shoe.

words.meaning: a small group chosen to make decisions
words.sentence: The committee met on Monday.
words.tip: Two m's, two t's, two e's.

words.meaning: a firm promise that something will happen
words.sentence: The shop gave a one-year guarantee.

words.meaning: to interest someone very much
words.sentence: Stars fascinate me.

words.meaning: giving off bright light, as some lamps and paints do
words.sentence: The classroom has fluorescent lights.

words.meaning: from another country
words.sentence: She is learning a foreign language.

words.meaning: lucky
words.sentence: We were fortunate to get tickets.

words.meaning: often
words.sentence: He frequently visits the library.

words.meaning: real, not fake
words.sentence: It is a genuine diamond.

words.meaning: the rules for how words are put together
words.sentence: Good grammar makes writing clear.

words.meaning: keeping clean to stay healthy
words.sentence: Good hygiene means washing your hands.

words.meaning: right now, without waiting
words.sentence: Please come immediately.

words.meaning: able to do things without help from others
words.sentence: She is a very independent girl.

words.meaning: the ability to learn, understand and think
words.sentence: The crow showed great intelligence.

words.meaning: to break into what someone is saying or doing
words.sentence: Please do not interrupt me.

words.meaning: not connected to the matter being talked about
words.sentence: That comment is irrelevant.

words.meaning: unhappy because you want what someone else has
words.sentence: He felt jealous of his friend's new bike.

words.meaning: the legal joining of two people as partners
words.sentence: They celebrated their marriage in the garden.

words.meaning: the study of numbers, shapes and patterns
words.sentence: She loves mathematics.

words.meaning: a period of one thousand years
words.sentence: A millennium is a thousand years.

words.meaning: strange and hard to explain
words.sentence: A mysterious light shone in the woods.

words.meaning: easy to see
words.sentence: The scar is hardly noticeable.

words.meaning: something that happens
words.sentence: Rain is a common occurrence here.

words.meaning: a chance to do something good
words.sentence: This is a great opportunity to learn.

words.meaning: the group of people who make the laws of a country
words.sentence: Parliament voted on the new law.

words.meaning: meant to last for a very long time
words.sentence: This marker leaves a permanent stain.

words.meaning: to make someone agree by giving reasons
words.sentence: She tried to persuade me to join.

words.meaning: to do with the body
words.sentence: Running is good physical exercise.

words.meaning: something that you own
words.sentence: Her bike is her most valued possession.
words.tip: Two s's, then two more s's.

words.meaning: an unfair opinion formed before knowing the facts
words.sentence: We should not judge people with prejudice.

words.meaning: to follow in order to catch, or to try to achieve
words.sentence: She wants to pursue a career in science.

words.meaning: a paper that shows you have paid
words.sentence: Keep the receipt in case you need to return it.

words.meaning: advice that something is good
words.sentence: I took her recommendation and read the book.

words.meaning: careful and thorough about doing your work
words.sentence: She is a conscientious student.

words.meaning: a system with many rules and officials
words.sentence: Getting the form approved meant fighting the bureaucracy.

words.meaning: made up of different kinds
words.sentence: The box held miscellaneous items.

words.meaning: a person you know slightly
words.sentence: He is an acquaintance, not a close friend.

words.meaning: a person who starts a business
words.sentence: The entrepreneur opened her first shop at nineteen.

words.meaning: a list of questions used to collect information
words.sentence: Please fill in the questionnaire.

words.meaning: careful watching of a person or place
words.sentence: The shop has camera surveillance.

words.meaning: the work of keeping something in good condition
words.sentence: The bridge is closed for maintenance.

words.meaning: the way a word is said aloud
words.sentence: Her pronunciation of French is excellent.

words.meaning: complex and advanced
words.sentence: The robot uses sophisticated sensors.

words.meaning: making you think of something from the past
words.sentence: The smell was reminiscent of summer holidays.

words.meaning: to do with speaking in a persuasive way
words.sentence: It was a rhetorical question, so no one answered.

words.meaning: a plan that lists when things will happen
words.sentence: The train schedule is on the wall.

words.meaning: an officer of middle rank in the army or police
words.sentence: The sergeant gave the orders.

words.meaning: a dark shape seen against a light background
words.sentence: A silhouette of a tree stood against the sunset.

words.meaning: happening at exactly the same time
words.sentence: The two goals were almost simultaneous.

words.meaning: serious and not smiling
words.sentence: The room was quiet and solemn.
words.tip: There is a silent 'n' at the end.

words.meaning: something you keep to remember a place or event
words.sentence: She bought a souvenir at the beach.

words.meaning: done naturally without planning
words.sentence: The crowd gave a spontaneous cheer.

words.meaning: a plan for winning or achieving something
words.sentence: Our strategy was to attack early.

words.meaning: small and delicate; not obvious
words.sentence: There was a subtle difference in taste.

words.meaning: to achieve what you wanted
words.sentence: Keep trying and you will succeed.

words.meaning: enough
words.sentence: We have sufficient food for everyone.

words.meaning: feeling that something is not right
words.sentence: He was suspicious of the strange email.

words.meaning: showing that you care about someone else's trouble
words.sentence: The teacher was sympathetic and kind.

words.meaning: a person's usual nature, such as calm or hot-headed
words.sentence: The horse has a gentle temperament.

words.meaning: complete and careful
words.sentence: She did a thorough job cleaning.

words.meaning: a very sad event
words.sentence: The flood was a tragedy for the town.

words.meaning: agreed by everyone
words.sentence: The vote was unanimous.

words.meaning: not needed
words.sentence: The extra paperwork was unnecessary.

words.meaning: watching carefully for danger
words.sentence: The guard stayed vigilant all night.

words.meaning: able to be seen
words.sentence: The stars are visible tonight.

words.meaning: easy to hurt or harm
words.sentence: Young birds are vulnerable to cats.

words.meaning: very strange
words.sentence: That is a weird noise.
words.tip: Weird is weird: e before i.

words.meaning: to keep back and not give
words.sentence: The bank may withhold the money.

words.meaning: to give way, or to produce a crop
words.sentence: Drivers must yield to people crossing.

words.meaning: patterns or shades that help something hide
words.sentence: The lizard uses camouflage to hide.

words.meaning: very exciting and making you feel full of energy
words.sentence: The ride was exhilarating.

words.meaning: a list of the books and sources used in a piece of work
words.sentence: Add a bibliography at the end of the essay.

words.meaning: seeing or hearing something that is not really there
words.sentence: A high fever can cause a hallucination.

words.meaning: an illness of the lungs
words.sentence: He was in bed with pneumonia.
words.tip: The 'p' at the start is silent.

words.meaning: a meeting at an agreed time and place
words.sentence: We planned a rendezvous at the station.

words.meaning: the way a person or an animal acts
words.sentence: Her kind behavior made everyone smile.

words.meaning: the quality that makes things funny
words.sentence: He has a good sense of humor.

words.meaning: to arrange things in a neat and sensible order
words.sentence: Please organize your books by size.

words.meaning: to suddenly understand or notice something
words.sentence: I realize now that I left my bag at school.

words.meaning: a unit for measuring how much liquid there is
words.sentence: The bottle holds one liter of water.

words.meaning: a metal covering that protected a knight in battle
words.sentence: The knight wore shiny armor.

words.meaning: a kind thing you do to help someone
words.sentence: Can you do me a favor?

words.meaning: protection against an attack
words.sentence: The castle wall was a strong defense.
